subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bundled dashboard widget write-back capability now, and should persisted widget state use the existing plugin keyed-state/SQLite seam rather than per-widget JSON files?
rationale: The feature is useful and roadmap-aligned, but it changes iframe-to-parent trust, persisted state ownership, and dashboard/plugin API contracts that automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor with storage and security design
options.body: Proceed after the Wave 1 dashboard base lands, requiring a reviewed bridge contract, manifest capability semantics, plugin-state/SQLite storage, and adversarial tests.

options.title: Defer under the roadmap
options.body: Keep the issue open under the Wave 2 tracker until the dashboard base PRs settle and maintainers can evaluate the added write-back surface.

options.title: Reject bundled write-back for now
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide stateful custom widgets should stay outside bundled OpenClaw until a separate plugin or ClawHub path proves demand.

recommendation.title: Sponsor with storage and security design
recommendation.body: Proceed after the Wave 1 dashboard base lands, requiring a reviewed bridge contract, manifest capability semantics, plugin-state/SQLite storage, and adversarial tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the current Control UI plugin-tab seam that this dashboard capability would extend.
